guide.title: How to create a service account key
guide.step1_1: Open GCP Console -> IAM -> Service Accounts -> Create
guide.step1_2: Name it (e.g. ice-deployer), click Create and Continue
guide.step1_3: Grant two roles (click "+ Add Another Role" for the second):
guide.step1_3_role1: Owner — for creating and managing resources
guide.step1_3_role2: Service Usage Admin — required for ICE to auto-enable GCP APIs (Cloud Run, Storage, etc.) during deployment.
guide.step2_1: Click the newly created service account
guide.step2_3: Click Add Key -> Create new key -> JSON
guide.step2_4: Download the file and paste its contents into the field above

computeContainer.name: Scalable Backend
computeContainer.tooltip: Auto-scaling containerized service supporting any runtime — Node.js, Python, Go, Java, .NET, Rust. Runs behind a load balancer with health checks, rolling deploys, and configurable min/max instances.

computeWorker.name: Worker
computeWorker.tooltip: Long-running background process that picks up jobs from a queue. Use for image/video processing, email sending, PDF generation, data imports, or any work that shouldn't block an API response.

computeServerlessFunction.name: Serverless Function
computeServerlessFunction.tooltip: Serverless function (Lambda, Cloud Functions, Azure Functions) that runs your code in response to events. No servers to manage — scales automatically from zero to thousands of concurrent executions. Pay only for compute time used.

computeFunctionCompute.name: Function Compute
computeFunctionCompute.tooltip: Alibaba Cloud Function Compute — serverless execution environment for event-driven code. Supports Node.js, Python, Java, and Go. Auto-scales from zero with pay-per-execution pricing.

computeOCIFunctions.name: OCI Functions
computeOCIFunctions.tooltip: Oracle Cloud Functions — serverless platform built on the open-source Fn Project. Supports multiple languages, runs in Docker containers, and integrates with OCI Events and API Gateway.

computeDOAppPlatform.name: App Platform
computeDOAppPlatform.description: DigitalOcean PaaS. Git push to deploy.
computeDOAppPlatform.tooltip: DigitalOcean App Platform — fully managed PaaS. Connect your GitHub repo and deploy with git push. Supports static sites, web services, workers, and background jobs with automatic HTTPS.

computeCronJob.name: Cron Job
computeCronJob.description: Runs on a schedule. Reports, cleanup, syncs.
computeCronJob.tooltip: Runs on a cron schedule. Use for nightly reports, database cleanup, cache warming, billing cycles, or periodic data syncs. Runs once and exits — not a long-lived process.

computeStaticSite.name: Static Site
computeStaticSite.tooltip: Pre-built HTML/CSS/JS served from a CDN. Ideal for React, Vue, or Angular SPAs. Blazing fast globally — files are cached at edge locations. No server needed.

computeSSRSite.name: SSR Site
computeSSRSite.tooltip: Server-side rendered app (Next.js, Nuxt, Remix). Pages render on the server for fast first paint and SEO. Supports API routes, middleware, and dynamic content. CDN caches static assets.

networkVPC.name: VPC
networkVPC.tooltip: Virtual Private Cloud — an isolated private network that contains your subnets and resources. Provides network-level isolation, custom IP ranges, route tables, and security boundaries. All production workloads should run inside a VPC.

networkSubnet.name: Subnet
networkSubnet.tooltip: A subdivision of a VPC that isolates resources into public or private segments. Public subnets have internet access; private subnets are shielded behind NAT. Use subnets to separate frontend, backend, and data tiers.

networkPublicEndpoint.name: Public Endpoint
networkPublicEndpoint.description: Public HTTPS entry point with managed SSL.
networkPublicEndpoint.tooltip: Single block that exposes your services to the internet. Set a domain (example.com) and toggle HTTPS to auto-provision a managed SSL certificate. Connect to one or more services and set a Subdomain on each edge to route api.example.com → API service, app.example.com → static site, etc. Replaces the old separate Internet + Custom Domain blocks.

networkCustomDomain.name: Custom Domain
networkCustomDomain.description: Route a domain to publicly-facing services.
networkCustomDomain.tooltip: Wires a root domain to one or more publicly-facing services that already have their own public URL (Firebase Hosting, Cloud Run with --allow-unauthenticated, AWS Amplify). Set a domain (example.com) and connect to one or more targets with a Subdomain on each edge — blank = root, api = api.example.com, etc. After deploy you'll see DNS records to add at your registrar. Use Secure Group instead if your services need to be inside a private network.

networkSecureGroup.name: Secure Group
networkSecureGroup.description: Private VPC + subnet with built-in load balancer.
networkSecureGroup.tooltip: A composite block: a private VPC + subnet PLUS a public load balancer that exposes services inside it. Drop your compute blocks (Cloud Run, containers, databases) inside the Secure Group, then add subdomain routes at the top of the block to expose them. Each route gets its own connection port — drag from a row to a child to wire that subdomain to that service. HTTPS + managed SSL provisioned automatically. Use this when your services need to live in a private network with controlled public access.

networkGateway.name: Gateway
networkGateway.tooltip: API Gateway that sits between the internet and your backend services. Handles request routing, authentication, rate limiting, CORS, and request/response transformation. Includes WAF and TLS termination.

databasePostgreSQL.name: PostgreSQL
databasePostgreSQL.tooltip: Managed PostgreSQL database with automatic backups, replication, and failover. Best for structured data with complex queries, joins, and transactions. Supports JSON, full-text search, and extensions like PostGIS.

databaseMySQL.name: MySQL
databaseMySQL.tooltip: Managed MySQL database — the most widely deployed open-source relational database. Optimized for read-heavy workloads, web applications, and e-commerce. Simple, reliable, and well-understood.

databaseMongoDB.name: MongoDB
databaseMongoDB.tooltip: Managed MongoDB document database. Stores data as flexible JSON-like documents — no fixed schema required. Great for content management, catalogs, user profiles, and rapidly evolving data models.

databaseDynamoDB.name: DynamoDB
databaseDynamoDB.tooltip: AWS DynamoDB — fully managed NoSQL key-value and document database. Single-digit millisecond performance at any scale. Supports on-demand and provisioned capacity, global tables, and DynamoDB Streams for change data capture.

databaseFirestore.name: Firestore
databaseFirestore.description: Google Cloud document DB. Real-time sync.
databaseFirestore.tooltip: Google Cloud Firestore — serverless document database with real-time sync and offline support. Data is organized into collections and documents. Ideal for mobile and web apps that need live data updates across clients.

databaseCosmosDB.name: Cosmos DB
databaseCosmosDB.tooltip: Azure Cosmos DB — globally distributed multi-model database. Supports NoSQL, MongoDB, Cassandra, Gremlin, and Table APIs. Guaranteed single-digit millisecond reads and writes with five consistency levels and turnkey global replication.

databaseTablestore.name: Tablestore
databaseTablestore.tooltip: Alibaba Cloud Tablestore — serverless NoSQL wide-column store optimized for time-series, IoT, and metadata. Auto-scales with no capacity planning needed.

databaseAutonomousDB.name: Autonomous DB
databaseAutonomousDB.tooltip: Oracle Cloud Autonomous Database — self-driving, self-securing, self-repairing. Automated tuning, patching, and scaling. Supports OLTP, data warehousing, JSON, and APEX workloads.

databaseDOManagedDB.name: Managed Database
databaseDOManagedDB.tooltip: DigitalOcean Managed Database — simple, reliable managed databases. Supports PostgreSQL, MySQL, and Redis with automatic failover, backups, and end-to-end encryption.

databaseRedis.name: Redis
databaseRedis.tooltip: Managed Redis in-memory data store. Use for caching API responses, session storage, rate limiting counters, real-time leaderboards, and pub/sub messaging. Sub-millisecond latency.

messagingSQS.name: SQS
messagingSQS.tooltip: AWS Simple Queue Service — fully managed message queue. Messages are stored durably and delivered at-least-once. Supports FIFO ordering and dead-letter queues for failed messages. Scales automatically.

messagingSNS.name: SNS
messagingSNS.tooltip: AWS Simple Notification Service — fan-out pub/sub messaging. One message can trigger multiple subscribers (SQS queues, Lambda functions, HTTP endpoints, email, SMS). Great for event-driven architectures.

messagingRabbitMQ.name: RabbitMQ
messagingRabbitMQ.tooltip: Open-source message broker supporting AMQP, MQTT, and STOMP protocols. Flexible routing with exchanges, queues, and bindings. Runs anywhere — cloud or self-hosted on Kubernetes.

messagingTopic.name: Event Stream
messagingTopic.tooltip: High-throughput event streaming platform (Kafka, Kinesis). Ordered, durable log of events that multiple consumers can read independently. Use for real-time analytics, event sourcing, and data pipelines.

messagingCloudPubSub.name: Cloud Pub/Sub
messagingCloudPubSub.tooltip: Google Cloud Pub/Sub — fully managed real-time messaging service. Publish messages to topics and deliver to multiple subscribers globally. Supports push and pull delivery, dead-letter topics, and exactly-once processing.

messagingServiceBus.name: Service Bus
messagingServiceBus.tooltip: Azure Service Bus — enterprise-grade message broker with queues and publish-subscribe topics. Supports sessions, transactions, dead-lettering, and scheduled delivery. Ideal for decoupling applications and building reliable distributed systems.

storageBucket.name: Storage
storageBucket.tooltip: Object storage (S3, GCS, Azure Blob, Alibaba OSS, OCI Object Storage, DO Spaces) for files, images, videos, backups, and static assets. Virtually unlimited capacity with high durability. Supports versioning, lifecycle policies, and pre-signed URLs.

storageOSS.name: OSS
storageOSS.description: Alibaba Cloud object storage. China-optimized CDN.
storageOSS.tooltip: Alibaba Cloud Object Storage Service — massively scalable object storage with China-optimized CDN integration. Supports Standard, IA, Archive, and Cold Archive storage classes.

storageOCIObjectStorage.name: OCI Object Storage
storageOCIObjectStorage.description: Oracle Cloud enterprise object storage. Tiered.
storageOCIObjectStorage.tooltip: Oracle Cloud Object Storage — enterprise-grade with automatic tiering between Standard and Archive tiers. High durability with built-in redundancy across fault domains.

storageDOSpaces.name: Spaces
storageDOSpaces.tooltip: DigitalOcean Spaces — simple S3-compatible object storage with built-in CDN. Flat pricing, no egress surprises. Great for static assets, backups, and user uploads.

securityIdentity.name: Auth
securityIdentity.tooltip: Managed identity and authentication service (Cognito, Firebase Auth, Entra ID). Handles user signup, login, MFA, social login (Google, GitHub), JWT tokens, and role-based access control.

securitySecret.name: Secrets
securitySecret.tooltip: Secrets manager for storing API keys, database passwords, OAuth tokens, and certificates. Encrypted at rest, accessed via API, with automatic rotation and audit logging.

securityWAF.name: WAF
securityWAF.description: Web Application Firewall. DDoS & injection protection.
securityWAF.tooltip: Web Application Firewall that protects APIs and web apps from common exploits — SQL injection, XSS, DDoS attacks, bot traffic, and OWASP Top 10 vulnerabilities. Sits in front of your API gateway or load balancer.

securityCertificate.name: SSL Certificate
securityCertificate.tooltip: Managed SSL/TLS certificate for HTTPS. Auto-provisions and auto-renews certificates for your custom domains. Free with most cloud providers (ACM, Managed SSL, Key Vault).

aiLLMGateway.name: LLM Gateway
aiLLMGateway.description: LLM API proxy. Rate limiting + fallback.
aiLLMGateway.tooltip: Proxy/router for LLM API calls (OpenAI, Anthropic, Cohere). Centralizes API key management, adds rate limiting, request caching, cost tracking, and automatic fallback between models.

aiVectorDB.name: Vector DB
aiVectorDB.tooltip: Vector database for storing and querying embeddings. Powers semantic search, RAG (retrieval-augmented generation), recommendation engines, and image similarity. Supports Pinecone, pgvector, Weaviate, and more.

aiModelServing.name: ML Model
aiModelServing.tooltip: Managed endpoint for serving ML models in production. Handles model versioning, A/B testing, auto-scaling, and GPU allocation. Supports PyTorch, TensorFlow, and custom containers.

analyticsDataWarehouse.name: Data Warehouse
analyticsDataWarehouse.tooltip: Columnar data warehouse for analytical queries over terabytes of data. Run complex SQL aggregations, joins, and window functions in seconds. Supports BigQuery, Redshift, and Synapse.

analyticsSearch.name: Search
analyticsSearch.tooltip: Full-text search and analytics engine. Index documents and query them with fuzzy matching, faceted search, autocomplete, and relevance scoring. Powers search bars, log analysis, and real-time dashboards.

monitoringLog.name: Logs
monitoringLog.tooltip: Centralized logging and monitoring. Collects logs from all services, enables search and filtering, triggers alerts on errors or anomalies, and provides performance dashboards.

monitoringTerminal.name: Log Terminal
monitoringTerminal.tooltip: Terminal-style log viewer with color-coded levels, auto-scroll, and click-to-copy. Streams live logs from connected services.

sourceRepository.name: GitHub Repo
sourceRepository.description: Source code. Connect to a service to deploy.
sourceRepository.tooltip: GitHub repository as a deployment source. Specify repo, branch, build command, and output directory. Connect to any service to define where its code comes from. Supports auto-deploy on push.

configEnvironment.name: Env Variables
configEnvironment.tooltip: Environment variables and configuration values. Define key-value pairs like DATABASE_URL, API keys, and feature flags. Connect to services that consume them.
